operations.credit_rule_for_next_section: Only concepts with state USABLE may be assumed in S06. PARTIAL, MENTION_ONLY, MISCONCEPTION_RISK and MISSING receive no automatic prerequisite credit.

effective_campaign_state.note_on_counts: Running local counts only. Mandatory global passes may merge recurring root causes, reject false positives or change severities when later dependency evidence is available.

S06_entry_watchlist: S06 is the first roadmap section allowed to teach lists, tuples, dictionaries, sets, slicing, unpacking, nested structures and structure choice. Prior uses in S02-S05 remain MENTION_ONLY and cannot be treated as learned.
for is USABLE from S04 and may support collection traversal, but range/enumerate/zip/while/comprehensions are not fully creditable due S04 defects.

return, docstrings, pure-function concept and LEGB are USABLE from S05; function_definition and parameter/argument binding remain PARTIAL because S05 did not cleanly isolate the definition-call-binding-return trace.
Mutable defaults remain MISCONCEPTION_RISK; S06 should explicitly connect mutability/aliasing/copy to the default-object behavior shown in S05 rather than assuming the rule was understood.
Preconditions remain MISCONCEPTION_RISK because S05 conflated caller obligations with runtime checks.
Type hints and domain errors remain PARTIAL; S06 should not build collection pedagogy on nested typing constructs merely because S05 displayed Tuple/Optional.
Exceptions/try-except/raise remain MENTION_ONLY until S09 unless a deliberate curriculum repair establishes an earlier micro-model.
String-method mechanics remain MENTION_ONLY until S07 despite heavy S05 normalizer examples.
I/O injection remains MISCONCEPTION_RISK because S05 demonstrated transformation-function injection rather than I/O dependency injection.
Behavior-preserving refactor remains MISCONCEPTION_RISK because S05's canonical example never executed the pre-refactor implementation.
CP-N1-B/CASO identifiers remain a persistent widow-term family unless expanded globally.
